sections.title: Short questions
sections.instructions: Answer all questions in this section.

questions.stem: Which SQL clause filters groups after aggregation?
questions.marking_notes: HAVING filters groups; WHERE filters rows before grouping.

questions.stem: A candidate key is any superkey that is not a proper superset of another candidate key.
questions.marking_notes: A candidate key is a minimal superkey. The stem describes minimality incompletely / incorrectly.

questions.stem: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using a natural join rather than an inner join with an explicit ON condition.
questions.answer: Advantage: less verbose when join columns share names. Disadvantage: accidental joins on extra same-named columns; harder to see intent.
questions.marking_notes: 2 marks advantage, 2 marks disadvantage, 2 marks for a precise contrast.

questions.stem: A relation R(A, B, C, D) has FDs {A → B, B → C, AC → D}.

parts.stem: Compute the closure of A. Show working.
parts.marking_notes: Start from A; add B; then C via B → C; then D via AC → D.

parts.stem: State whether A is a candidate key, and explain using your closure.
parts.answer: Yes. A+ contains all attributes of R, and no proper subset of A exists.
parts.marking_notes: 4 marks for using A+ = R; 4 marks for minimality / candidate-key definition.

questions.stem: A clinic stores Patient(pid, name, dob) and Appointment(aid, pid, when, room). A patient may have many appointments.

parts.stem: Write SQL to list each patient's name and the number of appointments they have, including patients with none.
parts.answer: SELECT p.name, COUNT(a.aid) AS n FROM Patient p LEFT JOIN Appointment a ON p.pid = a.pid GROUP BY p.pid, p.name;
parts.marking_notes: LEFT JOIN required; COUNT on appointment key not *; GROUP BY patient identity.

parts.stem: Explain two integrity constraints you would declare, and one anomaly that appears if they are omitted.
parts.answer: FK Appointment.pid → Patient.pid; PK on Appointment.aid (and maybe UNIQUE(pid, when)). Without FK, orphan appointments; without keys, duplicate identity rows.
parts.marking_notes: 5 marks for two plausible constraints; 5 marks for a matching anomaly.
